**A model answer.** Your numbers will differ — the point is that you read them out of the file rather than recalling them.

> 1. **`baseURL`** — set to the banking app, `https://test-automation-banking.vercel.app/`. It is what makes `page.goto('/')` work in a spec without repeating the host.
> 2. **`testMatch`** — the course repo widens the default so the `weekN/generated/` files are picked up. The default alone is `**/*.@(spec|test).?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` — the `.spec.ts` rule you prove for yourself on [Day 4 - Implementation](/learn/w1/d4/p3).
> 3. **`projects`** — `chromium` is active; `firefox` and `webkit` are present but commented out, which is why every run so far has opened exactly one browser.

**What makes an answer good** is that all three came from text you actually opened. The habit matters more than the answers: a config you have read is a config you can change, and from Week 3 onward you change it a lot.

3:
**A model answer.** There is no single right configuration; there is a defensible one.

> **Folder layout.** I would split by type from the start, into `tests/e2e/` and `tests/api/`, rather than one flat `tests/`. Renaming folders later means touching every `testMatch`, every CI job and everyone's muscle memory. Splitting on day one costs nothing.
>
> **GitHub Actions.** Yes, turn it on. The generated workflow is a reasonable starting point and a suite nobody runs on a push stops being trusted within a month.
>
> **Browsers.** Start with Chromium only. Three browsers on day one triples the runtime and, on a young suite, triples the failures you have to triage — almost none of which are real cross-browser bugs. Add Firefox and WebKit once the suite is stable.
>
> **Evidence settings.** Keep `trace: 'retain-on-failure'`. It costs nothing on a green run and is the difference between debugging a CI failure and guessing at it.

**The shape of a good answer** is a reason attached to each choice. "All three browsers because more coverage is better" is a position; "Chromium first because early failures are mostly my bugs, not browser bugs" is an argument.
